instructions: Rinse the rice in a medium pot with cold water, swirling and draining until the water runs almost clear. Add 1 3/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered until you serve.

Scrape the skin off the burdock with the back of a knife. Don't use a peeler. Cut the roots into 2 inch lengths, then slice each piece lengthwise into thin planks. Stack the planks and cut them into thin matchsticks.
Transfer the burdock into a large bowl of cold water as you cut and soak it for 10 minutes, changing the water once halfway.
Meanwhile, peel the carrot and cut it into matchsticks the same size. In a small bowl, stir together the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Drain the burdock, rinse it under cold water, and drain it well.
Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over medium heat. Add the burdock and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until it's halfway softened.
Add the carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until both are tender but still have a bite.
Pour in the soy sauce mixture. Cook, stirring, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the liquid is gone and the vegetables look glossy.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sesame seeds. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
method_notes: Lead is Just One Cookbook's kinpira gobo (4.73 from 112): scrape, julienne, soak the burdock, sesame oil, burdock first then carrot, then soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar cooked down until glossy. Amounts are scaled by about 1.75 to make a main with rice rather than a side for 4, and the optional dried chili is left out. Japanese Cooking 101 adds dashi and Chopstick Chronicles uses brown sugar; both are optional here, so it stays vegan. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 to 4 days, and they freeze for up to a month (Just One Cookbook).
